question: If P : Q = 6 : 11, Q : R = 5 : 4, and R : S = 9 : 7, find P : Q : R : S.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the column multiplication method for continuous ratios:

P = 6 × 5 × 9 = 270

Q = 11 × 5 × 9 = 495

R = 11 × 4 × 9 = 396

S = 11 × 4 × 7 = 308

**∴ The correct answer is 270 : 495 : 396 : 308.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ P : Q = 6 : 11

⇒ Q : R = 5 : 4

⇒ R : S = 9 : 7

 Visual Method: Fill empty spaces with adjacent numbers

**Calculations:**

⇒ Equalize Q in the first two ratios (LCM of 11 and 5 is 55).

⇒ P : Q = (6 × 5) : (11 × 5) = 30 : 55

⇒ Q : R = (5 × 11) : (4 × 11) = 55 : 44

⇒ Combining them, P : Q : R = 30 : 55 : 44

⇒ Now, equalize R in P : Q : R and R : S (LCM of 44 and 9 is 396).

⇒ P : Q : R = (30 × 9) : (55 × 9) : (44 × 9) = 270 : 495 : 396

⇒ R : S = (9 × 44) : (7 × 44) = 396 : 308

⇒ Combine all to get the final ratio:

⇒ P : Q : R : S = 270 : 495 : 396 : 308

**∴ The correct answer is 270 : 495 : 396 : 308.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Ratio

When two or more ratios are multiplied together, it is called a compound ratio. For a:b and c:d, the compound ratio is (a × c) : (b × d).

Duplicate & Sub-duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is a² : b². The sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

Componendo and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). This rule is heavily used to simplify complex algebraic fraction statements.
